title: Tteokbokki
subtitle: Korean spicy rice cakes in gochujang sauce
excerpt: Tteokbokki (spicy stir-fried rice cakes) is one of the most popular Korean street foods: cylindrical rice cakes simmered in a sweet, spicy gochujang sauce with fish cake and spring onion. The rice cakes are chewy and dense; the sauce is deeply flavoured. It is ready in under 20 minutes.
sourceNotes: Tteokbokki (떡볶이) is a Korean street food originally made with a soy-based sauce. The spicy gochujang version became popular in the 1950s and is now the dominant form. It is sold from pojangmacha (street food carts) throughout South Korea and is a national comfort food. Fish cakes (eomuk) are the classic addition.

content.text: Korean cylindrical rice cakes (garaetteok) are sold fresh, frozen, or vacuum-packed in Asian grocery stores. Fresh or vacuum-packed are best: frozen rice cakes become grainy if not defrosted properly. If the rice cakes are very dry or hard, soak them in cold water for 30 minutes before cooking.

items.prepNote: Korean cylindrical rice cakes (garaetteok), fresh or vacuum-packed

content.text: Make the sauce: whisk together the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, fish sauce, and garlic with 600 ml of water in a wide saucepan. Bring to the boil.

Add the rice cakes. Stir to separate them. Cook at a vigorous simmer, stirring occasionally, for 12 to 15 minutes until the rice cakes are soft and chewy and the sauce has reduced to a thick, glossy coating. Add the spring onion in the last 3 minutes.
Serve immediately in bowls, scattered with sesame seeds. Tteokbokki thickens as it cools and the rice cakes harden. Eat it fresh from the pan.

items.symptom: Rice cakes are still hard after 15 minutes
items.cause: Rice cakes were dry or cold from the fridge
items.fix: Soak the rice cakes in cold water for 30 minutes before cooking. Continue simmering and add a splash of hot water to loosen the sauce if it becomes too thick.
